name: Village of Ardsley
gaps: Ardsley has no schedule table: bulk rules are separate sections per district (Ch. 200, Arts. III-VIA)
County lists R-2 / R-3 building coverage as 26% / 34%; current code says 25% / 28% (amended L.L. 4-2003)
R-4 sets only street setback (30 ft) and side/rear yards by what they abut (30 ft next to residential, 20 ft next to business); recorded the residential-adjacent figure
CCH-1/CCH-2 are cluster sites (8-12 acres) with R-3 building standards and a 75 ft perimeter buffer; no per-lot yards recorded
RO: one-family homes follow all R-3 standards (§ 200-64.1C); multifamily follows B-1 standards with 40 ft / 4 stories / 40% coverage (not recorded)
No local pool setbacks found (Ch. 178 covers fencing only)

wetlands.summary: § 200-93A(1): structures, grading, filling, vegetation removal etc. within wetlands, water bodies, watercourses and a 25 ft buffer need a Planning Board permit.

steep_slopes.summary: § 200-93A(2): Planning Board permit to disturb steep slopes (25%+ with at least 10 ft dimension and area >= 10% of the district minimum lot or actual lot, whichever is less).

trees.summary: Ch. 185 regulates street trees; in subdivisions, removal of trees over 6 in. diameter (at 4 ft) needs Planning Board approval.

stormwater.summary: Ch. 171: SWPPP for land development activity, which includes any new building, construction on vacant or demolished lots, or 1+ acre of disturbance.

adu.summary: Art. XIIB: one ADU per lot in R-1/R-2/R-3 with a one-family home, owner-occupied, 300 to the lesser of 800 sf or 30% of the house, max 2 bedrooms, no short-term rental; village cap of 50 ADUs.

general.accessory_structures: Accessory buildings: per-district distances to front/side/rear boundaries (R-1 40/30/40, R-2 30/20/20, R-3 20/15/15 ft), max 20 ft and 2 stories. Unroofed terraces may come within 4 ft of a lot line (§ 200-85A); porches count as building.
general.pools: Ch. 178: pools must be fenced at least 4 ft high; no separate zoning setback found.
general.notes: Front yard must equal the average of the adjacent lots' front yards, min 20 ft and max 40 ft (§ 200-85E). Lots under 100 ft deep may reduce the rear yard by 1/4 of the shortfall, min 15 ft (§ 200-85F).

R-1.name: R-1 One-Family Residential

max_building_coverage.note: All buildings incl. porches and decks

max_impervious_coverage.note: Gross land coverage: all buildings, structures and paved/gravel surfaces (§ 200-83C); under 7,500 sf it is 2,500 sf or 40%, whichever is greater; +10 sf per foot of front setback beyond the minimum; special permit maximum 2,800/47%, 3,550+14%, 8,100+14%

max_floor_area.note: Basic permitted floor area for the house plus accessory buildings, any district (§ 200-83B); under 7,500 sf it is 2,400 sf or 40% of lot, whichever is greater. Planning Board special permit can raise it to 2,760/46%, 3,450+28%, 4,150+10%, 7,150+5%. Floor area includes roofed porches/decks, carports and garages

accessory.notes: Accessory buildings max 20 ft and 2 stories; no minimum distance to main building

R-1.source: §§ 200-7 to 200-12; § 200-83 house size and gross land coverage; § 200-89 corner lots
R-1.notes: 30 ft and 2 stories above grade plane (24 ft for low-slope roofs); highest roof point max 38 ft (pitched) / 32 ft (low-slope) above average grade along any wall. Corner lots: side-street side yard equals the front yard (§ 200-89). Lot width is mean lot width.
